+# Process-group failure patterns
+
+Code that reads the global parallel grid usually works when every model in the job uses that
+grid. It goes wrong when a component runs on a grid of its own, for example:
+
+- an encoder and a language model with different parallelism;
+- a separate inference layout;
+- a second model in the same job.
+
+This page lists the patterns behind those failures. For each one it shows what the pattern looks
+like, what goes wrong, and how to write it instead.
+
+For why the global grid is being deprecated, see
+[Deprecating `parallel_state`](parallel-state-deprecation.md). For how to build a collection for
+your own grid, see
+[Building a `ProcessGroupCollection` for your own grid](process-group-collection.md).
+
+## Two facts behind most failures
+
+**An unset field reads as `None`.** `ProcessGroupCollection` returns `None` for any field that was
+never set:
+
+```python
+pgs = ProcessGroupCollection(tp=tp_group)
+hasattr(pgs, "pp")  # True
+pgs.pp              # None
+```
+
+A missing field therefore looks the same as a field set to `None`, and a `hasattr` check never
+fails. `vars(pgs)` contains only the fields that were set.
+
+**`None` means different things to different callees:**
+
+- Megatron Core helpers treat `None` as a group of one rank. `get_pg_size(None)` is 1,
+  `get_pg_rank(None)` is 0, and `is_pp_first_stage(None)` and `is_pp_last_stage(None)` are both
+  true.
+- `torch.distributed` treats `group=None` as the default group, which contains every rank in the
+  job.
+
+A component that runs on its own grid then fails in one of two ways:
+
+- **Another grid is initialized globally.** The global read succeeds and returns that grid's ranks.
+  Nothing raises; the results are wrong, or the job hangs.
+- **No global grid exists.** The read raises, or falls through to the default group.
+
+[Testing on a grid of its own](#testing-on-a-grid-of-its-own) shows how to catch both.
+
+## 1. A silent default collection
+
+```python
+class MyLayer(MegatronModule):
+    def __init__(self, config, pg_collection=None):
+        super().__init__(config=config)
+        if pg_collection is None:
+            pg_collection = ProcessGroupCollection.use_mpu_process_groups()
+        self.tp_group = pg_collection.tp
+```
+
+**What goes wrong.** A caller that forgets to pass its collection gets the global grid's groups,
+with no signal. If the global grid belongs to another model, the layer runs on that model's ranks.
+With no global grid, `use_mpu_process_groups()` raises even for groups the layer never uses,
+because by default it builds every field.
+
+**Write instead.** Take the collection from the caller. A fallback for existing callers may stay
+while they migrate. It must do four things:
+
+- carry a comment that marks it as a fallback;
+- warn, naming the component and the release that removes the fallback;
+- build only the fields the component reads;
+- check that those fields are set.
+
+In Megatron Core, `resolve_process_groups()` does the last three:
+
+```python
+        # Compatibility fallback for callers that do not pass a collection yet.
+        pg_collection = resolve_process_groups(
+            pg_collection,
+            owner=type(self).__name__,
+            required=("tp",),
+            deprecated_in="0.21",
+            removed_in="0.23",
+        )
+```
+
+Outside Megatron Core, read the grid in a `global_process_group_fallback()` block instead. See
+[Fallbacks](parallel-state-deprecation.md#fallbacks-processgroupfallbackwarning).
+
+A hand-built collection that copies `parallel_state` accessors into the fields one by one is the
+same pattern, and needs the same treatment.
+
+## 2. A missing group that looks present
+
+```python
+        pp_group = pg_collection.pp if hasattr(pg_collection, "pp") else None  # always true
+        pp_rank = get_pg_rank(pp_group)  # an unset pp gives rank 0 on every stage
+```
+
+```python
+        assert hasattr(pg_collection, "dp_cp")  # never fails
+        torch.distributed.all_reduce(num_tokens, group=pg_collection.dp_cp)  # unset: every rank
+```
+
+**What goes wrong:**
+
+- A collection without `pp` makes every pipeline stage build the first stage's layers.
+- A reduction over an unset group runs over every rank in the job. For example, take a token count
+  that should be summed over the data-parallel ranks. On a TP=2 × PP=2 grid with one data-parallel
+  replica it is summed over 4 ranks instead, so the per-token loss and its gradients come out 4×
+  too small. A job with several grids hangs instead, because ranks outside the model never join the
+  collective.
+- An unset tensor-parallel group in inference makes `get_world_size(None)` return the size of the
+  whole job. An unset data-parallel group gives tensor-parallel peers different sampling seeds.
+
+**Write instead.** Check the fields once, when the component is built. Use `vars()`, so that an
+absent field raises and an explicit `None` keeps its meaning of "this axis is not used". Raise
+`ValueError` rather than asserting, because `python -O` removes asserts.
+
+```python
+        groups = vars(pg_collection)
+        missing = [name for name in ("tp", "pp") if name not in groups]
+        if missing:
+            raise ValueError(f"{type(self).__name__} needs {missing} in its pg_collection")
+        self.tp_group = groups["tp"]
+        self.pp_group = groups["pp"]  # None means no pipeline parallelism
+```
+
+## 3. A collective without the owner's group
+
+```python
+        fc1_input = copy_to_tensor_model_parallel_region(hidden_states)  # no group
+        ...
+        output = reduce_from_tensor_model_parallel_region(fc2_output)  # no group
+```
+
+The tensor-parallel mappings fall back to the global tensor-parallel group when `group` is `None`.
+The fallback emits a `ProcessGroupFallbackWarning` once per mapping, on every rank that reaches it,
+but it still selects the global group. Without an initialized global grid, the group stays `None`
+and the mapping fails.
+
+**What goes wrong.** The weights are sharded over the module's tensor-parallel group, but the
+gather or reduction runs over the global one. Depending on the layouts, this sums unrelated
+replicas, gathers the wrong number of shards (a shape error), or leaves each rank with another
+rank's sequence chunk.
+
+**Write instead.** Pass the group the module owns to every mapping and collective:
+
+```python
+        fc1_input = copy_to_tensor_model_parallel_region(hidden_states, group=self.tp_group)
+        ...
+        output = reduce_from_tensor_model_parallel_region(fc2_output, group=self.tp_group)
+```
+
+## 4. A global size or rank used in arithmetic
+
+```python
+        tp_size = parallel_state.get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size()
+        ep_size = parallel_state.get_expert_model_parallel_world_size()
+```
+
+**What goes wrong.** The number is right for the global grid and wrong for the component. Sizes
+and ranks feed shard shapes, padding multiples, RNG seed offsets, summation orders, and the choice
+of pipeline schedule:
+
+- A fused layer that checks the global size can take a single-rank path on a sharded grid.
+- An inference context pads to the global grid's multiple.
+- A pipeline-parallel model can be given the schedule for no pipelining.
+
+**Write instead.** Take the size or rank from the group or communicator the component already
+holds:
+
+```python
+        tp_size = get_pg_size(self.tp_group)
+        ep_size = get_pg_size(self.ep_group)
+```
+
+## 5. A pipeline rank that is not passed on
+
+```python
+    if config.pipeline_model_parallel_layout is not None:
+        return config.pipeline_model_parallel_layout.get_num_layers_to_build(
+            layer_type=LayerType.decoder, vp_stage=vp_stage  # pp_rank is not passed
+        )
+```
+
+**What goes wrong.** Without `pp_rank`, the layout uses the global pipeline rank. Under a global
+grid with one pipeline stage, a model on its own two-stage grid builds the first stage's layers,
+with the first stage's layer numbers, on every rank. Its checkpoint keys and its multi-token
+prediction placement are wrong too. A builder that holds the collection but does not pass the rank
+to the spec functions has the same effect.
+
+**Write instead.** Pass the rank from the owner's pipeline group through every layer of the call
+chain:
+
+```python
+        return config.pipeline_model_parallel_layout.get_num_layers_to_build(
+            layer_type=LayerType.decoder, vp_stage=vp_stage, pp_rank=get_pg_rank(pg_collection.pp)
+        )
+```
+
+## 6. Checkpoint metadata from the global grid
+
+```python
+    def sharded_state_dict(self, prefix="", sharded_offsets=(), metadata=None):
+        metadata = ensure_metadata_has_dp_cp_group(metadata)  # global DP x CP group
+        ...
+```
+
+**What goes wrong.** Replica ids decide which rank writes each shard. When the caller passes no
+metadata, which is common in tools, converters, exports and tests, the ids are computed over the
+global data-parallel ranks. On another grid, several ranks or no rank write a shard. Expert
+offsets computed from the global expert-parallel rank and size save optimizer state under another
+expert's name.
+
+**Write instead.** Fill the metadata from the owner's collection, with the same group that the
+global default selects (the GTP-remat-inclusive DP × CP group):
+
+```python
+        metadata = dict(metadata or {})
+        metadata.setdefault(
+            "dp_cp_group", self.pg_collection.dp_cp_gtp_remat or self.pg_collection.dp_cp
+        )
+```
+
+Pass expert ranks and sizes from the owner's expert groups in the same way.
+
+## 7. A collective over every rank
+
+```python
+        torch.distributed.all_reduce(flags, op=torch.distributed.ReduceOp.SUM)  # no group
+```
+
+The same happens when the group argument is a field that was never set, as described in
+[pattern 2](#2-a-missing-group-that-looks-present).
+
+**What goes wrong.** The collective includes every rank in the job. If some ranks never reach this
+code, for example encoder-only ranks or ranks serving rollouts, the job hangs. If they all reach it,
+statistics from different models are mixed. Reductions of FP8 scaling statistics, gradient norms
+and agreement flags are common cases.
+
+**Write instead.** Name the group whose ranks all run the code. If a collective really must span
+the whole job, say so in a comment, so that reviewers can tell it apart from a missing group.
+
+## 8. Changing shared state
+
+```python
+        if getattr(pg_collection, "dp", None) is None:
+            # Writes into the caller's collection.
+            pg_collection.dp = parallel_state.get_data_parallel_group()
+```
+
+```python
+        if tp_group is None:
+            tp_group = torch.distributed.new_group(ranks=[torch.distributed.get_rank()])  # per rank
+```
+
+**What goes wrong:**
+
+- Writing into a collection changes it for every later reader. A collection is usually shared by
+  every component of a model.
+- `torch.distributed.new_group` is collective. Every rank must call it with the same ranks in the
+  same order. Creating a different group on each rank desynchronizes group creation, and can hang.
+- State that only `initialize_model_parallel` creates is missing on a grid that was built without
+  it.
+- Teardown that does not destroy every group it created leaks communicators on each
+  initialize/destroy cycle.
+
+**Write instead:**
+
+- Keep derived groups in local variables, or raise when a required field is missing.
+- Create groups collectively. For one group per rank, use
+  `torch.distributed.new_subgroups_by_enumeration([[r] for r in range(world_size)])`.
+- Create shared state on first use instead of at grid initialization, as
+  `get_global_memory_buffer()` in `megatron.core.utils` does for the memory buffer.
+- Track every group that initialization creates, and destroy each one at teardown.
+
+## 9. A training loop that gives the collection only to the model
+
+```python
+    model = model_provider(pg_collection=pgs)
+    model = DistributedDataParallel(config, ddp_config, model)  # global groups
+    optimizer = get_megatron_optimizer(optimizer_config, [model])  # global groups
+    forward_backward_func = get_forward_backward_func()  # global pipeline size
+```
+
+**What goes wrong.** The model runs on its collection, but gradient synchronization, optimizer
+sharding, gradient norms, the pipeline schedule and RNG seeding use the global grid. The model then
+trains with gradients reduced over another grid's ranks.
+
+**Write instead.** Build one collection, then pass it to every component that runs on the grid, as
+in [Passing the collection](process-group-collection.md#passing-the-collection).
+
+## 10. Stage predicates and other non-group state
+
+```python
+    if parallel_state.is_pipeline_first_stage():
+        ...
+    vp_size = parallel_state.get_virtual_pipeline_model_parallel_world_size()
+```
+
+**What goes wrong.** Pipeline-stage predicates and the virtual-pipeline size have no collection
+field, so code that uses them only works on the global grid. Offline tools sometimes assign fake
+groups to `parallel_state`'s private module variables so that models can be built. A component
+that reads its own collection never sees those groups.
+
+**Write instead:**
+
+- Check stages against the owner's pipeline group, with the virtual-pipeline information passed
+  explicitly: `is_pp_first_stage(pp_group)` and `is_vp_first_stage(vp_stage, vp_size)` from
+  `megatron.core.pipeline_parallel.utils`.
+- Read the virtual-pipeline size from `config.virtual_pipeline_model_parallel_size`.
+- In tools, put the fake groups in a `ProcessGroupCollection` and pass it to the models, instead of
+  writing module variables.
+
+## 11. A fallback nobody sees
+
+```python
+        if tp_group is None:
+            if torch.distributed.get_rank() == 0:
+                warnings.warn("tp_group is None, using default tp group", DeprecationWarning)
+            tp_group = parallel_state.get_tensor_model_parallel_group()
+```
+
+**What goes wrong:**
+
+- Python hides `DeprecationWarning` outside `__main__`, so this warning is usually never shown.
+- Many fallbacks do not warn at all.
+- Training scripts often silence warnings on ranks other than 0. A fallback that only happens on
+  those ranks, for example on a pipeline stage that does not include rank 0, is then invisible.
+
+Users never learn that they depend on the global grid, so removing a fallback later breaks them
+without notice.
+
+**Write instead:**
+
+- Use a `FutureWarning` subclass, which Python shows by default.
+- Warn on every rank where the fallback happens, once per component.
+- Name the release that removes the fallback.
+- Make sure filters that quiet the other ranks let this category through.
+
+`resolve_process_groups()`, `warn_global_process_group_fallback()` and
+`global_process_group_fallback()` in `megatron.core.process_groups_config` do the first three,
+and the filters that training installs on ranks other than 0 let their category through. That
+category, `ProcessGroupFallbackWarning`, is their own, so that tests and strict runs can turn
+exactly these warnings into errors:
+
+```python
+with warnings.catch_warnings():
+    enable_strict_process_group_fallbacks()
+    build_model(pg_collection=pgs)  # raises if anything falls back to the global grid
+```
+
+## Testing on a grid of its own
+
+A test on the standard grid does not catch any of these patterns, because the global groups and
+the component's groups are the same. Instead:
+
+- **Use a different layout.** Initialize a global grid, then build the component on a collection
+  whose layout differs from it, for example TP=2 for the component under a global TP=1, or PP=2
+  under a global PP=1. Compare the result with the same component built on a matching global grid.
+- **Use no global grid.** Build the collection with `HyperCommGrid` without calling
+  `initialize_model_parallel`, and check that the component runs.
+- **Forbid global reads.** Patch the accessors the component should not call so that they raise:
+
+```python
+def _no_global_grid(*args, **kwargs):
+    raise AssertionError("read the global parallel grid")
+
+
+monkeypatch.setattr(parallel_state, "get_tensor_model_parallel_group", _no_global_grid)
+```
+
+Patch the name the component actually calls. A module that imported an accessor with
+`from megatron.core.parallel_state import ...` holds its own reference, so patch it in that module.

+def require_process_groups(
+    pg_collection: ProcessGroupCollection, names: Sequence[str], *, owner: str
+) -> Tuple[Any, ...]:
+    """Return the fields ``names`` of ``pg_collection`` in order, or raise if any is absent.
+
+    A field is present once the caller assigns it, including an explicit ``None``, which means
+    that the axis is off or that this rank is not a member of the group (for example ``embd`` on
+    a middle pipeline stage, or ``gtp_remat`` without GTP). A field that was never assigned also
+    reads as ``None`` through ``ProcessGroupCollection.__getattr__``, so a component cannot tell
+    it apart from an axis that is off; this function treats it as a caller error instead.
+
+    Args:
+        pg_collection: The collection the caller passed.
+        names: Fields that ``owner`` and the modules it builds read.
+        owner: Name of the class or function, used in error messages.
+
+    Returns:
+        The groups, one per name and in the order of ``names``.
+
+    Raises:
+        ValueError: ``pg_collection`` is None, a field is absent, or a field holds
+            ``torch.distributed.GroupMember.NON_GROUP_MEMBER``.
+        TypeError: ``pg_collection`` is a ``MultiModuleProcessGroupCollection``. Its modules
+            have different groups, so the caller selects the module's collection.
+    """
+    if pg_collection is None:
+        raise ValueError(f"{owner} requires a ProcessGroupCollection, got None.")
+    if isinstance(pg_collection, MultiModuleProcessGroupCollection):
+        raise TypeError(
+            f"{owner} requires the ProcessGroupCollection of one module, got a "
+            f"MultiModuleProcessGroupCollection with modules {list(pg_collection.keys())}. "
+            "Pass the collection of the module that owns these groups, for example "
+            "pg_collection.get_language_model_collection()."
+        )
+    groups = vars(pg_collection)
+    missing = [name for name in names if name not in groups]
+    if missing:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"{owner} requires pg_collection to set {', '.join(missing)}. Set a field to None "
+            "only when its axis is off or this rank is not a member of the group."
+        )
+    non_members = [
+        name for name in names if groups[name] is torch.distributed.GroupMember.NON_GROUP_MEMBER
+    ]
+    if non_members:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"{owner}: pg_collection sets {', '.join(non_members)} to NON_GROUP_MEMBER, which is "
+            "not a usable group. Use None on ranks that are not members of the group."

+### Strict process-group fallbacks
+
+A Megatron Core component that is not given its process groups falls back to
+the global ones in `parallel_state` and emits a `ProcessGroupFallbackWarning`.
+To make every fallback fail the test instead, pass the class to pytest's `-W`;
+pytest accepts a dotted class path:
+
+```bash
+uv run python -m torch.distributed.run --nproc-per-node 8 -m pytest -q \
+  -W error::megatron.core.process_groups_config.ProcessGroupFallbackWarning \
+  tests/unit_tests/models/test_gpt_model.py
+```
+
+- The same value works in a `@pytest.mark.filterwarnings(...)` marker.
+- `python -W` and `PYTHONWARNINGS` cannot name this class. Python resolves
+  them at startup, before torch can be imported, and ignores the option.
+- Each fallback warns once per process. One that already warned in an earlier
+  test, for example under `pytest.warns`, stays silent. A test that must
+  catch it calls `enable_strict_process_group_fallbacks()` from
+  `megatron.core.process_groups_config` inside `warnings.catch_warnings()`.
+- Training runs opt in with `--strict-process-group-fallbacks`.
+- The deprecated `parallel_state` accessors emit a separate
+  `ParallelStateDeprecationWarning`. `pyproject.toml` ignores it when a test
+  calls them, because tests use the global grid on purpose, and turns it into
+  an error when the caller is one of this repository's modules outside the
+  tests, such as `megatron.training.*`. Strict mode does not affect it. See
+  `docs/api-backwards-compatibility-check.md`.
+

+# Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+"""Share one model-parallel state across the A2A overlap tests of a module.
+
+destroy_model_parallel() releases the fused A2A (DeepEP and HybridEP) buffers together with
+the process groups they communicate over, and building a HybridEP buffer takes tens of
+seconds. Initializing and destroying model parallelism around every test would rebuild the
+buffer for every HybridEP case. Tests request their layout through ``shared_model_parallel``
+instead. It keeps the current state while tests request the same layout, and destroys it when
+a test requests a different layout, when a test fails on any rank, and at the end of the
+module.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+import megatron.core.parallel_state as ps
+from megatron.core.transformer.moe.token_dispatcher import nccl_ep_release_context
+from tests.unit_tests.test_utilities import Utils, clear_nvte_env_vars
+
+# (layout, model-parallel group) of the state initialized through this module, or None.
+_shared = None
+
+
+def _destroy_shared():
+    global _shared
+    _shared = None
+    Utils.destroy_model_parallel()
+
+
+def _use_layout(**layout):
+    """Initialize model parallelism with ``layout``, reusing the current state if it matches."""
+    global _shared
+    clear_nvte_env_vars()
+    if (
+        _shared is not None
+        and _shared[0] == layout
+        and ps.model_parallel_is_initialized()
+        and ps.get_model_parallel_group(check_initialized=False) is _shared[1]
+    ):
+        return
+    if _shared is not None:
+        _destroy_shared()
+    Utils.initialize_model_parallel(**layout)
+    _shared = (layout, ps.get_model_parallel_group())
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
+def shared_model_parallel():
+    """Return a function that initializes model parallelism with the given layout.
+
+    Its keyword arguments are those of Utils.initialize_model_parallel. The state persists
+    across the module's tests while they request the same layout.
+    """
+    yield _use_layout
+    if _shared is not None:
+        _destroy_shared()
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
+def _reset_shared_model_parallel(request):
+    """Reset per-test state between tests that share model parallelism."""
+    failures_before = request.session.testsfailed
+    yield
+    if _shared is None:
+        return
+    # All ranks must agree on whether to destroy the groups, and a test can fail on a
+    # subset of ranks. Destroy them after any failure, so later tests start fresh.
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    failed = torch.tensor(
+        [int(request.session.testsfailed > failures_before)], device=torch.cuda.current_device()
+    )
+    torch.distributed.all_reduce(failed, op=torch.distributed.ReduceOp.MAX)
+    if failed.item():
+        _destroy_shared()
+        return
+    # The NCCL EP context is sized by the first dispatch that bootstraps it, so each test
+    # bootstraps its own, as it did when every test destroyed model parallelism.
+    nccl_ep_release_context()
+    torch.cuda.empty_cache()

+    is_pp_first_stage,

+)

+)
+from tests.unit_tests.test_utilities import Utils
+
+SEQ_LEN = 32
+VOCAB_SIZE = 128
+NUM_MICROBATCHES = 4
+
+
+@contextmanager
+def _record_global_stage_queries():
+    """Record every query of the global grid for the CP size or the last pipeline stage.
+
+    The queries are recorded rather than raised: a stage that raised would stop sending
+    activations, and the next stage would wait for them forever.
+    """
+    queries = []
+
+    def _recorded(name, query):
+        def _record(*args, **kwargs):
+            queries.append(name)
+            return query(*args, **kwargs)
+
+        return _record
+
+    with ExitStack() as stack:
+        for name in ('get_context_parallel_world_size', 'is_pipeline_last_stage'):
+            query = getattr(schedules.parallel_state, name)
+            stack.enter_context(
+                mock.patch.object(schedules.parallel_state, name, _recorded(name, query))
+            )
+        yield queries
+
+
+def _interleaved_config():
+    """get_test_config's MLA + MoE model on PP=2 x VPP=2 with EP=2, one layer per stage."""
+    return MLATransformerConfig(
+        attention_backend="unfused",
+        pipeline_model_parallel_size=2,
+        virtual_pipeline_model_parallel_size=2,
+        expert_model_parallel_size=2,
+        # With two pipeline stages the interleaved schedule needs overlapped P2P communication.
+        overlap_p2p_comm=True,
+        batch_p2p_comm=False,
+        deterministic_mode=True,
+        bf16=True,
+        params_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        pipeline_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        num_layers=4,
+        hidden_size=512,
+        add_bias_linear=False,
+        num_attention_heads=128,
+        ffn_hidden_size=512,
+        kv_channels=128,
+        hidden_dropout=0.0,
+        attention_dropout=0.0,
+        multi_latent_attention=True,
+        num_moe_experts=8,
+        moe_grouped_gemm=True,
+        moe_router_dtype="fp32",
+        moe_token_dispatcher_type="alltoall",
+        overlap_moe_expert_parallel_comm=True,
+    )
+
+
+def _train_step(schedule, model_chunks, data, pg_collection, overlap, **schedule_kwargs):
+    """Run one forward-backward step; return the reduced losses and the gradients."""
+    config = model_chunks[0].config
+    config.overlap_moe_expert_parallel_comm = overlap
+    for chunk in model_chunks:
+        chunk.zero_grad()
+    with _record_global_stage_queries() as global_queries:
+        losses_reduced = schedule(
+            forward_step_func=forward_step_func,
+            data_iterator=[iter([data] * NUM_MICROBATCHES) for _ in model_chunks],
+            model=model_chunks,
+            num_microbatches=NUM_MICROBATCHES,
+            seq_length=SEQ_LEN,
+            micro_batch_size=1,
+            forward_only=False,
+            pg_collection=pg_collection,
+            **schedule_kwargs,
+        )
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    assert not global_queries, f"read parallel_state.{sorted(set(global_queries))}"
+    grads = {
+        f"{chunk_id}.{name}": param.grad.clone()
+        for chunk_id, chunk in enumerate(model_chunks)
+        for name, param in chunk.named_parameters()
+        if param.grad is not None
+    }
+    return [loss['lm loss'] for loss in losses_reduced], grads
+
+
+def _assert_same_step(reference, overlapped):
+    reference_losses, reference_grads = reference
+    losses, grads = overlapped
+    assert len(losses) == len(reference_losses)
+    for loss, reference_loss in zip(losses, reference_losses):
+        torch.testing.assert_close(loss, reference_loss)
+    assert grads.keys() == reference_grads.keys()
+    for name, grad in grads.items():
+        torch.testing.assert_close(grad, reference_grads[name], msg=name)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not is_te_min_version("1.9.0.dev0"), reason="Requires TE >= 1.9.0.dev0")
+@pytest.mark.skipif(Utils.world_size % 4 != 0, reason="needs a multiple of 4 ranks")
+class TestCombined1F1BProcessGroups:
+    """The overlapped step matches the plain step and never queries the global grid."""
+
+    def teardown_method(self, method):
+        Utils.destroy_model_parallel()
+        gc.collect()
+        torch.cuda.empty_cache()
+
+    def test_no_pipelining(self):
+        Utils.initialize_model_parallel(
+            tensor_model_parallel_size=1,
+            pipeline_model_parallel_size=1,
+            expert_model_parallel_size=4,
+        )
+        set_streams()
+        pg_collection = ProcessGroupCollection.use_mpu_process_groups()
+        with deterministic_mode():
+            config = get_test_config(
+                num_layers=2,
+                extra_kwargs={
+                    "moe_token_dispatcher_type": "alltoall",
+                    "overlap_moe_expert_parallel_comm": True,
+                },
+            )
+            model_chunks = [build_gpt_model(config, vocab_size=VOCAB_SIZE)]
+            data = build_input_data(seq_len=SEQ_LEN, vocab_size=VOCAB_SIZE)
+            schedule = schedules.forward_backward_no_pipelining
+            reference = _train_step(schedule, model_chunks, data, pg_collection, overlap=False)
+            overlapped = _train_step(schedule, model_chunks, data, pg_collection, overlap=True)
+
+        _assert_same_step(reference, overlapped)
+        assert len(overlapped[0]) == NUM_MICROBATCHES
+
+    def test_interleaved_pipelining(self):
+        Utils.initialize_model_parallel(
+            tensor_model_parallel_size=1,
+            pipeline_model_parallel_size=2,
+            virtual_pipeline_model_parallel_size=2,
+            expert_model_parallel_size=2,
+        )
+        set_streams()
+        pg_collection = ProcessGroupCollection.use_mpu_process_groups()
+        pp_group = pg_collection.pp
+        with deterministic_mode():
+            config = _interleaved_config()
+            vp_size = config.virtual_pipeline_model_parallel_size
+            # The pipeline sends activations in config.pipeline_dtype, so cast the chunks to
+            # bf16: the learned position embedding is created in fp32.
+            model_chunks = [
+                GPTModel(
+                    config=config,
+                    transformer_layer_spec=get_gpt_decoder_block_spec(
+                        config=config,
+                        use_transformer_engine=True,
+                        vp_stage=vp_stage,
+                        pp_rank=pp_group.rank(),
+                    ),
+                    vocab_size=VOCAB_SIZE,
+                    max_sequence_length=300,
+                    pre_process=is_vp_first_stage(vp_stage, vp_size)
+                    and is_pp_first_stage(pp_group),
+                    post_process=is_vp_last_stage(vp_stage, vp_size) and is_pp_last_stage(pp_group),
+                    share_embeddings_and_output_weights=False,
+                    vp_stage=vp_stage,
+                )
+                .bfloat16()
+                .cuda()
+                for vp_stage in range(vp_size)
+            ]
+            data = build_input_data(seq_len=SEQ_LEN, vocab_size=VOCAB_SIZE)
+            schedule = schedules.forward_backward_pipelining_with_interleaving
+            p2p_communicator = P2PCommunicator(pp_group=pp_group, config=config)
+            reference = _train_step(
+                schedule,
+                model_chunks,
+                data,
+                pg_collection,
+                overlap=False,
+                p2p_communicator=p2p_communicator,

+            overlapped = _train_step(
+                schedule,
+                model_chunks,
+                data,
+                pg_collection,
+                overlap=True,
+                p2p_communicator=p2p_communicator,
+            )
+
+        _assert_same_step(reference, overlapped)
+        # Only the last virtual stage of the last pipeline stage computes the loss.
+        assert len(overlapped[0]) == (NUM_MICROBATCHES if is_pp_last_stage(pp_group) else 0)

+"""Helpers for tests that check which group FP8/FP4 contexts reduce amaxes over."""
+
+from contextlib import ExitStack, contextmanager, nullcontext
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+import torch
+
+from megatron.core import parallel_state
+from megatron.core.enums import Fp8Recipe
+from megatron.core.process_groups_config import ProcessGroupCollection
+
+# The parallel_state accessors that return a global amax reduction group: the getter itself,
+# and the TP x CP and TP x DP x CP groups behind the collection fields tp_cp and tp_dp_cp.
+_GLOBAL_AMAX_GROUP_ACCESSORS = (
+    "get_amax_reduction_group",
+    "get_tensor_and_context_parallel_group",
+    "get_tensor_and_data_parallel_group",
+)
+
+
+def global_amax_group(tp_only_amax_red):
+    """Return the amax reduction group of the global parallel state."""
+    return parallel_state.get_amax_reduction_group(
+        with_context_parallel=True, tp_only_amax_red=tp_only_amax_red
+    )
+
+
+def global_amax_groups():
+    """Return a collection with the global grid's amax reduction groups, tp_cp and tp_dp_cp.
+
+    For tests that run modules on the global grid outside a model that holds a collection.
+    FP8/FP4 contexts given this collection reduce over the same groups as their deprecated
+    fallback, without its warning.
+    """
+    return ProcessGroupCollection.use_mpu_process_groups(required_pgs=["tp_cp", "tp_dp_cp"])
+
+
+def copy_of(group):
+    """Create a distinct communicator over the ranks of ``group``; every rank must call it."""
+    all_ranks = [None] * torch.distributed.get_world_size()
+    torch.distributed.all_gather_object(all_ranks, torch.distributed.get_process_group_ranks(group))
+    enumeration = [list(ranks) for ranks in sorted({tuple(ranks) for ranks in all_ranks})]
+    copy, _ = torch.distributed.new_subgroups_by_enumeration(enumeration)
+    return copy
+
+
+def with_copied_amax_groups(pg_collection=None):
+    """Set amax groups that match the global ones in ranks but not in identity.
+
+    A context that reads the global group instead of the collection's then fails an identity
+    check, although both groups reduce over the same ranks.
+    """
+    if pg_collection is None:
+        pg_collection = ProcessGroupCollection()
+    pg_collection.tp_cp = copy_of(global_amax_group(True))
+    pg_collection.tp_dp_cp = copy_of(global_amax_group(False))
+    return pg_collection
+
+
+@contextmanager
+def forbid_global_amax_group():
+    """Fail on any read of the global amax reduction group."""
+    error = AssertionError("the global amax reduction group was read")
+    with ExitStack() as stack:
+        for name in _GLOBAL_AMAX_GROUP_ACCESSORS:
+            stack.enter_context(patch.object(parallel_state, name, side_effect=error))
+        yield
+
+
+@contextmanager
+def record_amax_groups():
+    """Replace the Transformer Engine autocasts that Megatron opens with no-op contexts.
+
+    Yields a list that receives the ``fp8_group`` of every enabled autocast. Modules then run
+    unquantized, so the test does not depend on FP8 or FP4 hardware support.
+    """
+    import transformer_engine.pytorch as te_pytorch
+
+    from megatron.core.extensions import transformer_engine as te_extension
+
+    groups = []
+
+    def autocast(*args, **kwargs):
+        if kwargs.get("enabled"):
+            groups.append(kwargs["fp8_group"])
+        return nullcontext()
+
+    with (
+        patch.object(te_pytorch, "fp8_autocast", side_effect=autocast),
+        patch.object(te_extension, "fp8_autocast", side_effect=autocast),
+    ):
+        yield groups
+
+

+def _strided_tp_group(world_size):
+    """Pair rank r with rank r + world_size // 2, unlike the global grid's adjacent TP pairs."""
+    rank = torch.distributed.get_rank()
+    half = world_size // 2
+    tp_group = None
+    for first in range(half):
+        ranks = [first, first + half]
+        group = torch.distributed.new_group(ranks)
+        if rank in ranks:
+            tp_group = group
+    return tp_group
+

+@pytest.fixture
+def distributed():

+    Utils.initialize_distributed()
+    yield
+    Utils.destroy_model_parallel()

+
+@contextlib.contextmanager
+def _record_group_creation():
+    """Record the ranks of every process group created in the block, in creation order."""
+    created = []
+    new_group = dist.distributed_c10d.new_group
+
+    def recording_new_group(*args, **kwargs):
+        ranks = kwargs["ranks"] if "ranks" in kwargs else (args[0] if args else None)
+        created.append(None if ranks is None else sorted(ranks))
+        return new_group(*args, **kwargs)
+
+    with (
+        mock.patch.object(dist, "new_group", recording_new_group),
+        mock.patch.object(dist.distributed_c10d, "new_group", recording_new_group),
+    ):
+        yield created
+
+
+def _collection_without_expert_dp():
+    """Collection of a data-parallel-only grid (TP = PP = EP = 1) that leaves out expt_dp.
+
+    Creating groups is collective: call on every rank.
+    """
+    world_size = dist.get_world_size()
+    single_rank_group, _ = dist.new_subgroups_by_enumeration([[rank] for rank in range(world_size)])
+    return ProcessGroupCollection(
+        dp=dist.new_group(ranks=list(range(world_size))),
+        tp=single_rank_group,
+        pp=single_rank_group,
+        ep=single_rank_group,
+    )
+
+
+def _assert_same_on_every_rank(created):
+    created_on_every_rank = [None] * dist.get_world_size()
+    dist.all_gather_object(created_on_every_rank, created)
+    assert all(
+        created_on_rank == created_on_every_rank[0] for created_on_rank in created_on_every_rank
+    ), f"ranks created different process groups: {created_on_every_rank}"
+
+
+def _assert_later_groups_work():
+    """Create a group over every rank and reduce on it, as later setup code does."""
+    world_size = dist.get_world_size()
+    group = dist.new_group(ranks=list(range(world_size)))
+    names = [None] * world_size
+    dist.all_gather_object(names, group.group_name)
+    assert names == [names[0]] * world_size, f"ranks named the same group differently: {names}"
+    value = torch.tensor([float(dist.get_rank())], device="cuda")
+    dist.all_reduce(value, group=group)
+    assert value.item() == world_size * (world_size - 1) / 2
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("expt_dp", ["absent", "none"])
+def test_missing_expert_dp_group_is_created_alike_on_every_rank(distributed, expt_dp):
+    """Every rank creates the same single-rank groups, keeps its own, and stays in step."""
+    pg_collection = _collection_without_expert_dp()
+    if expt_dp == "none":
+        pg_collection.expt_dp = None
+    config = TransformerConfig(num_attention_heads=1, num_layers=1)
+    ddp_config = DistributedDataParallelConfig()
+
+    with _record_group_creation() as created:
+        groups = ProcessGroupCollection.setup_process_groups_for_ddp(
+            pg_collection, config, ddp_config
+        )
+
+    _assert_same_on_every_rank(created)
+    assert created, "expected an expert data-parallel group to be created"
+    expt_dp_group = groups['expt_dp_group']
+    assert dist.get_process_group_ranks(expt_dp_group) == [dist.get_rank()]
+    assert groups['intra_expt_dp_group'] is expt_dp_group
+
+    value = torch.tensor([float(dist.get_rank())], device="cuda")
+    dist.all_reduce(value, group=expt_dp_group)
+    assert value.item() == dist.get_rank()
+    _assert_later_groups_work()
+
+
+def test_ddp_without_expert_dp_group_keeps_group_creation_in_step(distributed):
+    """DistributedDataParallel on such a collection creates the same groups on every rank."""
+    pg_collection = _collection_without_expert_dp()
+    config = TransformerConfig(num_attention_heads=1, num_layers=1)
+    ddp_config = DistributedDataParallelConfig(overlap_grad_reduce=True, bucket_size=10000)
+    module = torch.nn.Sequential(torch.nn.Linear(8, 32), torch.nn.ReLU(), torch.nn.Linear(32, 8))
+
+    with _record_group_creation() as created:
+        ddp_model = DistributedDataParallel(
+            config, ddp_config=ddp_config, module=module.cuda(), pg_collection=pg_collection
+        )
+
+    _assert_same_on_every_rank(created)
+    assert dist.get_process_group_ranks(ddp_model.expt_dp_group) == [dist.get_rank()]
+    _assert_later_groups_work()
+
+
+def test_provided_expert_dp_group_is_used_without_creating_groups(distributed):
+    pg_collection = _collection_without_expert_dp()
+    pg_collection.expt_dp = pg_collection.dp
+    config = TransformerConfig(num_attention_heads=1, num_layers=1)
+    ddp_config = DistributedDataParallelConfig()
+
+    with _record_group_creation() as created:
+        groups = ProcessGroupCollection.setup_process_groups_for_ddp(
+            pg_collection, config, ddp_config
+        )
+
+    assert created == []
+    assert groups['expt_dp_group'] is pg_collection.expt_dp
+    assert groups['intra_expt_dp_group'] is pg_collection.expt_dp

+class _FakeGroup:
+    """Process-group stand-in with a rank, a size and the global ranks it spans."""
+
+    def __init__(self, rank, size, first_rank=0):
+        self._rank = rank
+        self.ranks = list(range(first_rank, first_rank + size))
+
+    def rank(self):
+        return self._rank
+
+    def size(self):
+        return len(self.ranks)

+def _forbid_global_process_groups(monkeypatch):
+    """Fail the test on any read of the global groups, ranks, sizes or pipeline stages."""
+
+    def fail(*args, **kwargs):
+        pytest.fail("Flextron code must not read the global parallel state")
+
+    for name, value in list(vars(parallel_state).items()):
+        if name.startswith(("get_", "is_pipeline_")) and callable(value):
+            monkeypatch.setattr(parallel_state, name, fail)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(

+        Mock(side_effect=AssertionError("supplied groups must not be rebuilt from globals")),
+    )

+

+def _use_global_fake_groups(monkeypatch, **groups):

+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        ProcessGroupCollection,
+        "use_mpu_process_groups",
+        staticmethod(lambda required_pgs=None: ProcessGroupCollection(**groups)),
+    )

+class _ShardedGroupedMLP(nn.Module):
+    """Grouped-MLP stand-in whose FC1 output holds this rank's shard of the FFN channels."""
+
+    def __init__(self, hidden_size, ffn_hidden_size, tp_group):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.tp_group = tp_group
+        self.hidden_size = hidden_size
+        shard_size = ffn_hidden_size // tp_group.size()
+        self.captured = None
+
+        class _FC1(nn.Module):
+            def forward(_self, x):
+                return x.new_ones(*x.shape[:-1], shard_size), None
+
+        self.linear_fc1 = _FC1()
+
+    def forward(self, hidden_states):
+        intermediate, _ = self.linear_fc1(hidden_states)
+        self.captured = intermediate.detach().clone()
+        return hidden_states, None
+
+

+def _strided_group(world_size):
+    """Pair rank r with rank r + world_size // 2, unlike any group of the default global grid."""
+    rank = torch.distributed.get_rank()
+    half = world_size // 2
+    own_group = None
+    for first in range(half):
+        ranks = [first, first + half]
+        group = torch.distributed.new_group(ranks)
+        if rank in ranks:
+            own_group = group
+    return own_group
+

+# Name suffixes of the parallel_state accessors that return a group, a rank or a size.
+_ACCESSOR_SUFFIXES = ("_group", "_groups", "_gloo", "_rank", "_ranks", "_world_size")
+
+_FUSED_MLP_CLASSES = [
+    pytest.param(
+        TEFusedMLP,
+        marks=pytest.mark.skipif(TEFusedMLP is None, reason="TE operation-based MLP unavailable"),
+        id="TEFusedMLP",
+    ),
+    pytest.param(
+        TEFusedMLPWithGroupedLinear,
+        marks=pytest.mark.skipif(
+            TEFusedMLPWithGroupedLinear is None or not is_te_min_version("2.14.0"),
+            reason="TEFusedMLPWithGroupedLinear requires Transformer Engine >= 2.14.0",
+        ),
+        id="TEFusedMLPWithGroupedLinear",
+    ),
+]
+
+
+@contextlib.contextmanager
+def _forbid_global_grid():
+    """Make the parallel_state group, rank and size accessors raise inside the block.
+
+    The TE extension imports some accessors by name, so they are replaced there as well.
+    """
+
+    def forbidden(name):
+        def read_global_grid(*args, **kwargs):
+            raise AssertionError(f"parallel_state.{name}() reads the global parallel grid")
+
+        return read_global_grid
+
+    with pytest.MonkeyPatch.context() as patch:
+        for name, value in list(vars(parallel_state).items()):
+            if callable(value) and name.startswith("get_") and name.endswith(_ACCESSOR_SUFFIXES):
+                stub = forbidden(name)
+                patch.setattr(parallel_state, name, stub)
+                if name in vars(te_ext):
+                    patch.setattr(te_ext, name, stub)
+        yield
+
+
+def _strided_tp_group(tp_size):
+    """Return this rank's TP group of a grid whose TP groups stride over the ranks.
+
+    The first grid dimension varies fastest, so consecutive ranks are in different TP groups,
+    unlike in the global grid.
+    """
+    world_size = torch.distributed.get_world_size()
+    grid = HyperCommGrid([world_size // tp_size, tp_size], ["dp", "tp"])
+    return grid.create_pg("tp")
+
+
+class TestTEFusedMLPTensorParallelGroup:
+
+    def teardown_method(self, method):
+        Utils.destroy_model_parallel()
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("fused_mlp_class", _FUSED_MLP_CLASSES)
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize(("global_tp_size", "tp_size"), [(2, 2), (1, 4)])
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("sequence_parallel", [False, True])
+    def test_matches_unfused_mlp_on_its_tp_group(
+        self, fused_mlp_class, global_tp_size, tp_size, sequence_parallel
+    ):
+        """The fused MLP communicates over its own TP group, not the global one."""
+        if Utils.world_size < 4 or Utils.world_size % tp_size:
+            pytest.skip(f"needs at least 4 ranks, divisible by {tp_size}")
+        Utils.initialize_model_parallel(tensor_model_parallel_size=global_tp_size)
+        model_parallel_cuda_manual_seed(123)
+
+        tp_group = _strided_tp_group(tp_size)
+        # gtp_remat=None stops the linear layers from looking up GTP groups in the global grid.
+        pg_collection = ProcessGroupCollection(tp=tp_group, gtp_remat=None)
+        config = TransformerConfig(
+            num_layers=1,
+            hidden_size=64,
+            ffn_hidden_size=128,
+            num_attention_heads=4,
+            tensor_model_parallel_size=tp_size,
+            sequence_parallel=sequence_parallel,
+            gated_linear_unit=True,
+            activation_func=F.silu,
+            add_bias_linear=False,
+            normalization="RMSNorm",
+            init_method_std=0.1,
+            hidden_dropout=0.0,
+            attention_dropout=0.0,
+        )
+        submodules = MLPSubmodules(
+            linear_fc1=TELayerNormColumnParallelLinear, linear_fc2=TERowParallelLinear
+        )
+
+        torch.manual_seed(1234)
+        hidden_states = torch.randn(16, 2, config.hidden_size, device="cuda")
+        if sequence_parallel:
+            hidden_states = hidden_states.chunk(tp_size)[tp_group.rank()]
+        output_grad = torch.randn_like(hidden_states)
+
+        results = []
+        with _forbid_global_grid():
+            mlp = MLP(
+                config,
+                submodules,
+                ffn_hidden_size=config.ffn_hidden_size,
+                tp_group=tp_group,
+                pg_collection=pg_collection,
+            )
+            fused_mlp = fused_mlp_class(
+                config,
+                submodules,
+                ffn_hidden_size=config.ffn_hidden_size,
+                tp_group=tp_group,
+                pg_collection=pg_collection,
+            )
+            with torch.no_grad():
+                for (name, param), (fused_name, fused_param) in zip(
+                    mlp.named_parameters(), fused_mlp.named_parameters()
+                ):
+                    assert name == fused_name
+                    fused_param.copy_(param)
+
+            for module in (mlp, fused_mlp):
+                inputs = hidden_states.clone().requires_grad_()
+                output, bias = module(inputs)
+                assert bias is None
+                output.backward(output_grad)
+                results.append(
+                    (output, inputs.grad, {n: p.grad for n, p in module.named_parameters()})
+                )
+
+        unfused_results, fused_results = results
+        # With sequence parallelism, the two paths sum some gradient terms in a different order.
+        torch.testing.assert_close(fused_results, unfused_results, rtol=1e-4, atol=1e-3)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not HAVE_TE, reason="Transformer Engine is not installed")
+class TestTEDotProductAttentionContextParallelGroup:
+
+    def setup_method(self, method):
+        Utils.initialize_model_parallel(1, 1)
+        model_parallel_cuda_manual_seed(123)
+
+    def teardown_method(self, method):
+        Utils.destroy_model_parallel()
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _tp_and_cp_groups():
+        world_size = torch.distributed.get_world_size()
+        grid = HyperCommGrid([1, 2, world_size // 2], ["tp", "cp", "dp"])
+        return grid.create_pg("tp"), grid.create_pg("cp")
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _build(pg_collection):
+        config = TransformerConfig(
+            num_layers=1, hidden_size=64, num_attention_heads=4, context_parallel_size=2
+        )
+        return TEDotProductAttention(
+            config,
+            layer_number=1,
+            attn_mask_type=AttnMaskType.causal,
+            attention_type="self",
+            pg_collection=pg_collection,
+        )
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("cp_field", ["absent", "none"])
+    def test_rejects_context_parallelism_without_cp_group(self, cp_field):
+        """A missing CP group must not turn every rank of the job into the CP ranks."""
+        if Utils.world_size % 2:
+            pytest.skip("needs an even number of ranks")
+        tp_group, _ = self._tp_and_cp_groups()
+        if cp_field == "absent":
+            pg_collection = ProcessGroupCollection(tp=tp_group)
+        else:
+            pg_collection = ProcessGroupCollection(tp=tp_group, cp=None)
+
+        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="pg_collection.cp"):
+            self._build(pg_collection)
+
+    def test_uses_the_cp_group_of_the_collection(self):
+        if Utils.world_size % 2:
+            pytest.skip("needs an even number of ranks")
+        tp_group, cp_group = self._tp_and_cp_groups()
+
+        attention = self._build(ProcessGroupCollection(tp=tp_group, cp=cp_group))
+
+        assert attention.cp_group is cp_group
+        assert attention.cp_global_ranks == torch.distributed.get_process_group_ranks(cp_group)

+# Same accessor selection as tools/check_process_group_usage.py.
+_ACCESSOR_SUFFIXES = ("_group", "_groups", "_gloo", "_rank", "_ranks", "_world_size")
+_NOT_ACCESSORS = {
+    "get_nccl_options",
+    "get_all_ranks",
+    "get_global_memory_buffer",

+class GlobalProcessGroupRead(Exception):
+    """Raised by a global process-group accessor inside `forbid_global_process_groups`.
+
+    Not an AssertionError, so code that treats AssertionError as "not initialized" cannot hide it.
+    """
+
+
+@contextlib.contextmanager
+def forbid_global_process_groups():
+    """Make every read of the global parallel grid raise inside the block.
+
+    Patches the `parallel_state` group, rank and size accessors, the copies that Megatron modules
+    imported by name (under any alias), and `ProcessGroupCollection.use_mpu_process_groups`.
+    """
+
+    def failing(name):
+        def fail(*args, **kwargs):
+            raise GlobalProcessGroupRead(f"read of the global parallel grid: {name}")
+
+        return fail
+
+    # Keyed by id() because module attributes need not be hashable; the values keep the
+    # functions alive, so an id cannot be reused while the block runs.
+    accessors = {
+        id(function): (name, function)
+        for name, function in vars(parallel_state).items()
+        if name.startswith("get_")
+        and name.endswith(_ACCESSOR_SUFFIXES)
+        and name not in _NOT_ACCESSORS
+    }
+    with pytest.MonkeyPatch.context() as patch:
+        for module in list(sys.modules.values()):
+            if not getattr(module, "__name__", "").startswith("megatron."):
+                continue
+            for attribute, value in list(getattr(module, "__dict__", {}).items()):
+                if id(value) in accessors:
+                    patch.setattr(module, attribute, failing(accessors[id(value)][0]))
+        patch.setattr(
+            ProcessGroupCollection,
+            "use_mpu_process_groups",
+            classmethod(failing("ProcessGroupCollection.use_mpu_process_groups")),
+        )
+        yield
+
+
+def _round_up(value, multiple):
+    return math.ceil(value / multiple) * multiple
+
+
+def _require_world_size_multiple_of(*sizes):
+    for size in sizes:
+        if Utils.world_size < size or Utils.world_size % size != 0:
+            pytest.skip(f"needs a world size that is a multiple of {size}")
+
+
+def _build_collection(tp_size, ep_size=1):
+    """A collection for an inference grid with its own TP size, built without global reads."""
+    return build_inference_pg_collection(
+        Utils.world_size, tp_size=tp_size, pp_size=1, cp_size=1, ep_size=ep_size, expt_tp_size=1
+    )
+

+def unit_rounders(monkeypatch):

+
+    The default rounders are multiples of every power-of-two TP size, which would hide padding
+    to the wrong TP size.

+    monkeypatch.setattr(DynamicInferenceContext, "REQUEST_ROUNDER", 1)

+class TestDynamicContextTensorParallelSize:
+    """`DynamicInferenceContext` pads to the TP size of its collection."""
+
+    def teardown_method(self, method):
+        Utils.destroy_model_parallel()
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("global_tp, context_tp", [(1, 2), (1, 4), (2, 1)])
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("num_speculative_tokens", [0, 2])
+    def test_step_padding_uses_collection_tp_size(
+        self, unit_rounders, global_tp, context_tp, num_speculative_tokens
+    ):
+        _require_world_size_multiple_of(global_tp, context_tp)
+        Utils.initialize_model_parallel(tensor_model_parallel_size=global_tp)
+        pg_collection = _build_collection(context_tp)
+        model_config = TransformerConfig(
+            params_dtype=torch.float32,
+            num_layers=2,
+            kv_channels=8,
+            num_attention_heads=4,
+            tensor_model_parallel_size=context_tp,
+        )
+        inference_config = InferenceConfig(
+            max_sequence_length=64,
+            buffer_size_gb=0.01,
+            block_size_tokens=16,
+            max_tokens=64,
+            max_requests=8,
+            num_speculative_tokens=num_speculative_tokens,
+            unified_memory_level=0,
+            pg_collection=pg_collection,
+        )
+        prompt_lengths = (5, 4, 4)
+        num_requests = len(prompt_lengths)
+
+        with forbid_global_process_groups():
+            context = DynamicInferenceContext(model_config, inference_config)
+
+            # Prefill step.
+            for request_id, prompt_length in enumerate(prompt_lengths):
+                context.add_request(
+                    DynamicInferenceRequest(
+                        request_id=request_id,
+                        prompt_tokens=torch.arange(prompt_length, device="cuda"),
+                        sampling_params=SamplingParams(num_tokens_to_generate=8),
+                    )
+                )
+            context.initialize_attention_state()
+            assert context.padded_active_token_count == _round_up(sum(prompt_lengths), context_tp)
+            assert context.padded_batch_dimensions.req_count == _round_up(num_requests, context_tp)
+
+            # Decode step for the same requests.
+            context.update_requests(
+                active_requests_mask=torch.ones(num_requests, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"),
+                new_tokens=torch.arange(num_requests, device="cuda"),
+                new_speculative_tokens=(
+                    torch.zeros(
+                        num_speculative_tokens, num_requests, dtype=torch.long, device="cuda"
+                    )
+                    if num_speculative_tokens > 0
+                    else None
+                ),
+            )
+            assert context.num_decode_requests == num_requests
+            context.initialize_attention_state()
+
+        padded_decode_requests = _round_up(num_requests, context_tp)
+        assert context.padded_batch_dimensions.decode_req_count == padded_decode_requests
+        assert context.padded_active_token_count == padded_decode_requests * (
+            num_speculative_tokens + 1
+        )

+"""In-tree scripts build their model on the groups that initialize_megatron registered.
+
+get_model_for_inference(), get_dynamic_inference_engine() and get_model() build the model on the
+collection they are given. The inference entry points, and every other script in this repository
+that calls megatron.training's get_model(), pass the registered one,
+parallel_state.get_registered_process_groups(); a caller that omits it falls back to the global
+grid with a ProcessGroupFallbackWarning. The tests run without torch.distributed, with stand-ins
+for the model builder and the checkpoint loader.
+"""

+# The folders whose code builds models; tests are not scanned.
+SCANNED_FOLDERS = ("megatron", "examples", "tools", "tasks")
+# The modules that scripts import megatron.training's get_model() from.
+GET_MODEL_MODULES = ("megatron.training", "megatron.training.training")
+# The groups that get_model_for_inference passes to load_checkpoint.
+CHECKPOINT_GROUPS = {
+    "tp_group": "tp",
+    "pp_group": "pp",
+    "dp_cp_group": "dp_cp",
+    "dp_group": "dp",
+    "expt_dp_group": "expt_dp",
+}
+

+    monkeypatch.setattr(process_groups_config, "_warned_global_process_group_fallbacks", set())
+
+
+class _Model:
+    def eval(self):
+        pass
+
+
+def _groups():
+    return ProcessGroupCollection(**{name: Mock() for name in CHECKPOINT_GROUPS.values()})
+
+
+def _forbid_the_shim(monkeypatch):
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        ProcessGroupCollection,
+        "use_mpu_process_groups",
+        Mock(side_effect=AssertionError("the groups were rebuilt from the global grid")),
+    )
+

+@pytest.fixture
+def inference(monkeypatch):
+    """Stand-ins for the arguments, the model builder and the checkpoint loader."""

+        fp8_recipe=None,
+        modelopt_enabled=False,
+    )
+    built, loaded = [], []
+
+    class Builder:
+        def build_distributed_models(self, pg_collection, wrap_with_ddp):
+            built.append(pg_collection)
+            return [_Model()]
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(utils, "get_args", lambda: args)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(utils, "get_model_builder", lambda args, pg_collection: Builder())
+    monkeypatch.setattr(utils, "load_checkpoint", lambda **kwargs: loaded.append(kwargs))
+    monkeypatch.setattr(utils, "_get_checkpoint_model_modifier", lambda args, keys: None)
+    return SimpleNamespace(args=args, built=built, loaded=loaded)
+

+        return prefix and f"{prefix}.{node.attr}"

+def _imported_module(node, package):
+    """Return the absolute name of the module that the ImportFrom ``node`` imports from.
+
+    A relative import resolves against ``package``, the name parts of the importing file's package.
+    """
+    if not node.level:
+        return node.module
+    parts = package[: max(len(package) - node.level + 1, 0)]
+    return ".".join(parts + ((node.module,) if node.module else ()))

+def _get_model_calls(path, root=REPO_ROOT):
+    """Return every call of megatron.training's get_model() in ``path``, in line order.
+
+    A call matches under any name that ``path`` imports get_model() or its module as, such as
+    ``get_training_model(...)`` or ``training.get_model(...)``, by an absolute import or by a
+    relative one, which resolves against the package of ``path`` under ``root``; a function of
+    another module that is also named get_model does not.
+    """
+    package = path.relative_to(root).parent.parts
+    tree = ast.parse(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+    functions, modules = set(), set(GET_MODEL_MODULES)
+    for node in ast.walk(tree):
+        if isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):
+            module = _imported_module(node, package)
+            for alias in node.names:
+                if module in GET_MODEL_MODULES and alias.name == "get_model":
+                    functions.add(alias.asname or alias.name)
+                elif f"{module}.{alias.name}" in GET_MODEL_MODULES:
+                    modules.add(alias.asname or alias.name)
+        elif isinstance(node, ast.Import):
+            modules.update(
+                alias.asname
+                for alias in node.names
+                if alias.asname and alias.name in GET_MODEL_MODULES
+            )
+    if ".".join(package + (path.stem,)) == "megatron.training.training":
+        functions.add("get_model")
+    calls = [
+        node
+        for node in ast.walk(tree)
+        if isinstance(node, ast.Call)
+        and (
+            (isinstance(node.func, ast.Name) and node.func.id in functions)
+            or (
+                isinstance(node.func, ast.Attribute)
+                and node.func.attr == "get_model"
+                and _dotted_name(node.func.value) in modules
+            )
+        )
+    ]
+    return sorted(calls, key=lambda call: call.lineno)

+        "training.get_model(provider)\n"

+    )

+"""Inference reaches the global process groups only through warned compatibility fallbacks.
+
+`InferenceConfig.resolve_pg_collection` is the one process-group boundary of the inference
+components, and the pipeline helpers in `megatron.core.inference.communication_utils` take the
+caller's pipeline group. Each fallback to the global grid emits one `ProcessGroupFallbackWarning`.
+Callers that pass their groups never warn, and every read of the global grid raises while their
+code runs. A collection that lacks a group inference reads, or sets a group that inference runs
+collectives on to None, is rejected before any component uses it.
+"""

+import sys
+import warnings
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest import mock
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from megatron.core import parallel_state, process_groups_config
+from megatron.core.hyper_comm_grid import HyperCommGrid
+from megatron.core.inference import communication_utils

+def forbid_global_process_groups():
+    """Make every read of the global parallel grid raise inside the block.

+    Patches the parallel_state accessors and stage predicates, the copies that Megatron modules
+    imported by name, and `ProcessGroupCollection.use_mpu_process_groups`.
+    """
+    # Keyed by id() because module attributes need not be hashable.
+    names = {
+        id(value): name
+        for name, value in vars(parallel_state).items()
+        if getattr(value, "__module__", None) == parallel_state.__name__
+        and (
+            name in _STAGE_PREDICATES
+            or (
+                name.startswith("get_")
+                and name.endswith(_ACCESSOR_SUFFIXES)
+                and name not in _NOT_ACCESSORS
+            )
+        )
+    }
+
+    def forbidden(name):
+        def read(*args, **kwargs):
+            raise GlobalProcessGroupRead(f"read of the global parallel grid: {name}")
+
+        return read
+
+    with pytest.MonkeyPatch.context() as patch:
+        for module_name, module in list(sys.modules.items()):
+            if module is None or module_name.split(".")[0] != "megatron":
+                continue
+            for attribute, value in list(vars(module).items()):
+                if id(value) in names:
+                    patch.setattr(module, attribute, forbidden(names[id(value)]))
+        patch.setattr(

+            classmethod(forbidden("ProcessGroupCollection.use_mpu_process_groups")),

+def _stand_in_collection(**overrides):
+    """Return a collection that sets every group inference reads, without creating any group.

+    The groups that inference runs collectives on are distinct stand-in objects, and the groups
+    whose axis may be off are None. An override replaces a group, and `_ABSENT` leaves it unset.

+    groups.update(dict.fromkeys(AXIS_GROUPS))

+    return ProcessGroupCollection(

+def _exchange_global_ranks(stage, num_stages, pp_group):
+    """Run the pipeline helpers on this rank's global rank.
+
+    Broadcasts from the last stage, then sends each stage's rank to the next stage. Returns the
+    broadcast value and the value received from the previous stage (None on the first stage).
+    """
+    rank = torch.full([2], float(torch.distributed.get_rank()), device="cuda")
+    is_last_stage = stage == num_stages - 1
+    broadcast = communication_utils.broadcast_from_last_pipeline_stage(
+        [2], torch.float32, tensor=rank if is_last_stage else None, pp_group=pp_group
+    )
+    received = None
+    if stage > 0:
+        received = torch.zeros(2, device="cuda")
+        communication_utils.recv_from_prev_pipeline_rank_(received, pp_group=pp_group)
+    if not is_last_stage:
+        communication_utils.send_to_next_pipeline_rank(rank, pp_group=pp_group)
+    return int(broadcast[0].item()), None if received is None else int(received[0].item())

+# The accessors that tools/check_process_group_usage.py counts.
+_ACCESSOR_SUFFIXES = ("_group", "_groups", "_gloo", "_rank", "_ranks", "_world_size", "_src_rank")
+_NOT_ACCESSORS = {
+    "get_nccl_options",
+    "get_all_ranks",
+    "get_global_memory_buffer",
+    "get_virtual_pipeline_model_parallel_rank",
+    "get_virtual_pipeline_model_parallel_world_size",
+}
+# Pipeline-stage predicates also read the global grid; the checker counts them as functions.
+_STAGE_PREDICATES = ("is_pipeline_first_stage", "is_pipeline_last_stage")

+
+class GlobalProcessGroupRead(Exception):
+    """A read of the global parallel grid inside `forbid_global_process_groups`.
+
+    Not an AssertionError, so code that treats AssertionError as "not initialized" cannot hide it.
+    """
+
+
+@contextlib.contextmanager
+def forbid_global_process_groups():
+    """Make every read of the global parallel grid raise inside the block.
+
+    Patches the parallel_state accessors and stage predicates, the copies that Megatron modules
+    imported by name, and `ProcessGroupCollection.use_mpu_process_groups`.
+    """
+    # Keyed by id() because module attributes need not be hashable.
+    names = {
+        id(value): name
+        for name, value in vars(parallel_state).items()
+        if getattr(value, "__module__", None) == parallel_state.__name__
+        and (
+            name in _STAGE_PREDICATES
+            or (
+                name.startswith("get_")
+                and name.endswith(_ACCESSOR_SUFFIXES)
+                and name not in _NOT_ACCESSORS
+            )
+        )
+    }
+
+    def forbidden(name):
+        def read(*args, **kwargs):
+            raise GlobalProcessGroupRead(f"read of the global parallel grid: {name}")
+
+        return read
+
+    with pytest.MonkeyPatch.context() as patch:
+        for module_name, module in list(sys.modules.items()):
+            if module is None or module_name.split(".")[0] != "megatron":
+                continue
+            for attribute, value in list(vars(module).items()):
+                if id(value) in names:
+                    patch.setattr(module, attribute, forbidden(names[id(value)]))
+        patch.setattr(
+            ProcessGroupCollection,
+            "use_mpu_process_groups",
+            classmethod(forbidden("ProcessGroupCollection.use_mpu_process_groups")),
+        )
+        yield
+
+

+class _MetadataRecorder(torch.nn.Module):
+    """Records the checkpoint metadata that its parent passes to it."""
+
+    def __init__(self, pg_collection=None):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.pg_collection = pg_collection
+        self.metadata = None
+
+    def sharded_state_dict(self, prefix="", sharded_offsets=(), metadata=None):
+        self.metadata = metadata
+        return {}
+
+
+def _collection_without(field, state, **groups):
+    """Return a collection of ``groups`` in which ``field`` is unset or set to None."""
+    if state == "unset":
+        del groups[field]
+    else:
+        groups[field] = None
+    return ProcessGroupCollection(**groups)

+class TestOptimizerReplicaId:

+        pg_collection = ProcessGroupCollection(tp=_Group(1, 2), pp=_Group(2, 4), dp_cp=_Group(3, 8))

+
+    def test_gtp_remat_group_extends_the_tensor_parallel_rank(self):
+        pg_collection = ProcessGroupCollection(
+            tp=_Group(1, 2), pp=_Group(), dp_cp=_Group(), gtp_remat=_Group(1, 2)
+        )
+        assert _get_replica_id(pg_collection) == (1 * 2 + 1, 0, 0)
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("gtp_remat", ["unset", "none"])
+    def test_gtp_remat_unset_or_none_is_off(self, gtp_remat):
+        groups = dict(tp=_Group(1, 2), pp=_Group(), dp_cp=_Group())
+        if gtp_remat == "none":

+        assert _get_replica_id(ProcessGroupCollection(**groups)) == (1, 0, 0)
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("field", ["tp", "pp", "dp_cp"])
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("state", ["unset", "none"])

+        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=f"pg_collection to set {field}"):

+    def test_rejects_no_collection(self):

+    Modules that imported an accessor by name hold their own reference, so those are patched too.

+            continue

+

+            ):

+        raise AssertionError("read of the global grid: use_mpu_process_groups")

+    patch.setattr(ProcessGroupCollection, "use_mpu_process_groups", classmethod(forbid_shim))

+    """Make the global TP accessors and the collection shim raise, including by-name imports."""
+    for name in dir(parallel_state):
+        if not name.startswith(("get_tensor_model_parallel", "get_expert_tensor_parallel")):

+

+                getattr(module, "__dict__", {}).get(name) is original
+            ):

+
+    def forbid_shim(cls, *args, **kwargs):

+
+    patch.setattr(ProcessGroupCollection, "use_mpu_process_groups", classmethod(forbid_shim))

+# Copyright (c) 2026, NVIDIA CORPORATION. All rights reserved.
+
+"""LLaVA shards its language-model input over the groups of its own collection."""
+
+import sys
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from megatron.core import parallel_state
+from megatron.core.hyper_comm_grid import HyperCommGrid
+from megatron.core.models.multimodal.llava_model import LLaVAModel
+from megatron.core.process_groups_config import ProcessGroupCollection
+from tests.unit_tests.test_utilities import Utils
+
+
+def _forbid_global_tp(patch):
+    """Make the global TP accessors raise, including by-name imports of them."""
+    for name in dir(parallel_state):
+        if not name.startswith("get_tensor_model_parallel"):
+            continue
+        original = getattr(parallel_state, name)
+
+        def forbid(*args, _name=name, **kwargs):
+            raise AssertionError(f"read of the global grid: parallel_state.{_name}")
+
+        for module in list(sys.modules.values()):
+            if getattr(module, "__name__", "").startswith("megatron.") and (
+                getattr(module, "__dict__", {}).get(name) is original
+            ):
+                patch.setattr(module, name, forbid)
+
+
+def _make_sequence_parallel_model(pg_collection):
+    """Build only the state that sequence-parallel input sharding reads."""
+    model = object.__new__(LLaVAModel)
+    torch.nn.Module.__init__(model)
+    model.pre_process = True
+    model.post_process = True
+    model.context_parallel_lm = 1
+    model.sequence_parallel_lm = True
+    model.tensor_model_parallel_size_lm = pg_collection.tp.size()
+    model.tp_comm_overlap_lm = False
+    model.pg_collection = pg_collection
+    return model
+
+
+@pytest.mark.internal
+@pytest.mark.skipif(
+    Utils.world_size < 2 or Utils.world_size % 2 != 0, reason="needs an even number of ranks"
+)
+def test_sequence_parallel_input_is_split_over_model_tp_group(monkeypatch):
+    """Embeddings go to the model's TP=2 group even though the global grid has TP=1."""
+    Utils.initialize_model_parallel(tensor_model_parallel_size=1)
+    grid = HyperCommGrid([2, Utils.world_size // 2], ["tp", "dp"])
+    try:
+        tp_group = grid.create_pg("tp")
+        model = _make_sequence_parallel_model(ProcessGroupCollection(tp=tp_group))
+        sequence_length, batch_size, hidden_size = 8, 2, 4
+        combined_embeddings = (
+            torch.arange(sequence_length * batch_size * hidden_size, device="cuda")
+            .view(sequence_length, batch_size, hidden_size)
+            .float()
+            .requires_grad_(True)

+
+"""The multimodal context-parallel gather resolves its group once, in the forward.
+
+Its backward reduce-scatters over the group the forward gathered over, so a caller that omits
+the group reads the global grid once, with a warning, and never in the backward.
+"""
+
+import warnings
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from megatron.core import parallel_state, process_groups_config
+from megatron.core.models.multimodal.context_parallel import (
+    GatherFromContextParallelRanks,
+    gather_from_context_parallel_ranks,
+)
+from megatron.core.process_groups_config import ProcessGroupFallbackWarning
+from tests.unit_tests.test_utilities import (
+    Utils,
+    forbid_global_process_groups,
+    new_group_with_same_ranks,
+)
+
+OWNER_MESSAGE = "GatherFromContextParallelRanks was called without `cp_group`"
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
+def fresh_warning_registry(monkeypatch):
+    """Each test observes the first fallback warning of every owner."""
+    monkeypatch.setattr(process_groups_config, "_warned_global_process_group_fallbacks", set())
+
+
+def _local_tensor(cp_rank):
+    # [batch, seq, hidden]; each CP rank holds a different slice of the sequence.
+    return torch.full(
+        (1, 4, 8), float(cp_rank + 1), dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda", requires_grad=True
+    )
+
+
+def _gather_and_backward(local_t, cp_group=None, *, forbid_backward_reads=False):
+    gathered = gather_from_context_parallel_ranks(local_t, 0, cp_group=cp_group)
+    weights = torch.arange(gathered.numel(), device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32).view_as(gathered)
+    if forbid_backward_reads:
+        with forbid_global_process_groups():
+            (gathered * weights).sum().backward()
+    else:
+        (gathered * weights).sum().backward()

+"""The MFSDP v2 optimizer names experts by its model's own expert-parallel layout."""
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from megatron.core.optimizer import OptimizerConfig
+from megatron.core.optimizer.fully_sharded_optimizer import FullyShardedOptimizer
+from megatron.core.process_groups_config import ProcessGroupCollection
+from megatron.core.transformer.fsdp_dtensor_checkpoint import get_global_unique_param_name
+from tests.unit_tests.test_utilities import Utils
+from tests.unit_tests.transformer.test_fsdp_dtensor_expert_offsets import (
+    expert_model,
+    forbid_global_expert_parallel_reads,
+)
+
+NUM_LOCAL_EXPERTS = 2
+
+
+def build_optimizer(model):
+    """Build the MFSDP v2 optimizer for ``model`` behind a wrapper like the MFSDP v2 one.
+
+    The wrapper has no ``pg_collection`` of its own, so the optimizer has to find the
+    model's collection through ``module``.
+    """
+    model_chunk = torch.nn.Module()
+    model_chunk.module = model
+    model_chunk.config = model.config
+    model_chunk.ddp_config = SimpleNamespace()
+    return FullyShardedOptimizer(
+        torch.optim.SGD(model_chunk.parameters(), lr=1.0),
+        OptimizerConfig(lr=1.0, use_distributed_optimizer=False),
+        grad_scaler=None,
+        init_state_fn=None,
+        model_chunks=[model_chunk],
+    )
+
+
+class TestFullyShardedOptimizerExpertNames:
+
+    def setup_method(self, method):
+        if Utils.world_size < 4 or Utils.world_size % 2 != 0:
+            pytest.skip("needs a global EP=2 grid that differs from an EP=world grid")
+        # The global grid pairs ranks along EP.
+        Utils.initialize_model_parallel(expert_model_parallel_size=2)
+
+    def teardown_method(self, method):
+        Utils.destroy_model_parallel()
+
+    def test_names_follow_the_model_expert_layout(self):
+        world_size, rank = Utils.world_size, torch.distributed.get_rank()
+        model = expert_model(NUM_LOCAL_EXPERTS, num_moe_experts=NUM_LOCAL_EXPERTS * world_size)
+        # The model's own EP group spans every rank.
+        model.pg_collection = ProcessGroupCollection(
+            ep=torch.distributed.new_group(ranks=list(range(world_size)))
+        )
+        local_experts = model.decoder.layers[0].mlp.experts.local_experts
+
+        with forbid_global_expert_parallel_reads():
+            optimizer = build_optimizer(model)
+
+        offset = NUM_LOCAL_EXPERTS * rank
+        assert [optimizer._param_to_fqn[expert.weight] for expert in local_experts] == [
+            f'module.decoder.layers.0.mlp.experts.local_experts.{offset + i}.weight'
+            for i in range(NUM_LOCAL_EXPERTS)
+        ]
+
+    def test_names_on_the_standard_grid_match_the_global_layout(self):
+        model = expert_model(NUM_LOCAL_EXPERTS, num_moe_experts=NUM_LOCAL_EXPERTS * 2)
+        model.pg_collection = ProcessGroupCollection.use_mpu_process_groups(required_pgs=['ep'])
+
+        optimizer = build_optimizer(model)
+
+        for param, name in optimizer._param_to_fqn.items():
+            assert name == get_global_unique_param_name(optimizer.model_chunks, param)
+
+    def test_dense_model_needs_no_collection(self):
+        model = torch.nn.Linear(2, 2, bias=False)
+        model.config = SimpleNamespace(num_moe_experts=None)
+
+        optimizer = build_optimizer(model)
+
+        assert optimizer._param_to_fqn == {model.weight: 'module.weight'}

+"""``clip_qk`` reduces the maximum attention logits over the group its caller passes."""
+
+import warnings
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest import mock
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from megatron.core import parallel_state, process_groups_config
+from megatron.core.optimizer.qk_clip import clip_qk
